assessment: The diagnosis says board WIDTH binds: mean 3.638 bodies by turn 6 against stack 003's five-body bar, finisher-plus-second-wave assembled 39.5%. So the ten leads with the one closer the worst axis can see (sweepers 0), then width and the field's consensus engine gaps — Silverback Elder 61%, Soul of the Harvest 59%, Glademuse 50%, The Great Henge 45% of recorded lists, all absent here. The back of the list is doors, not deficits: Seedborn Muse is a confirmed Game Changer that moves the computed floor to exactly the target, and Springheart Nantuko / Nissa, Resurgent Animist sit in the build's pool file carrying a recorded two-card infinite. No entry is premised on flashing a finisher: stack 005 refuted the end-step Craterhoof, and stack 006 verified that end-step BODIES attack at dawn — the ambush is for creatures and traps, the kill is a main-phase act.

ten.why: Sweepers is the deck's worst measured axis at 0 and the diagnosis names Whiptongue as the one closer the axis can see; it wipes every flier on ETB — the exact attack the trap suite cannot block — and Radagast flashes it for {3}{G} into a declared air strike.
ten.unlocks: A board reset that is itself a metronome body: the sweeper the 99 lacks without sweeping the 35 creatures the plan needs.

ten.why: The thinnest engine component: finisher plus second wave is 39.5% by turn 6 and the goldfish means 3.638 bodies against the five-body bar; on this 36-land base Avenger makes six-plus Plants at once, and stack 006 says an end-step Avenger's tokens all attack at dawn.
ten.unlocks: The widest one-card second wave in the colour — one Avenger turn makes any Stampede or Ibex X lethal instead of close.

ten.why: The diagnosis measured that only Beast Whisperer draws ungated on the creature plan — every other engine gates on power, combat or deaths; Soul draws on every nontoken body with no gate, on a 6/6 trample frame that keeps the greatest-power anchor Stampede and Ibex read when Old Fat Spider leaves. 59% of recorded Radagast lists run it.
ten.unlocks: A second ungated per-body draw engine, so the metronome pays a card even when the board's power is small.

ten.why: The field's top add at 61% of recorded lists, and it answers the diagnosis's interaction reading directly: the trap suite is combat-facing only, while Elder destroys an artifact or enchantment on every creature cast — one answer per turn cycle in a deck that casts a creature on every turn, no combat required.
ten.unlocks: Interaction that scales with the deck's own metronome: four creature casts a round is four Naturalizes, or lands, or life.

ten.why: The diagnosis names Henge as the only backup for the Selvala single point of failure (drawn 13.2% by turn 6, nothing in the pool covers her): a draw per nontoken body plus {G}{G} a turn, and any power-4 board discounts it toward five mana. 45% of recorded lists run it.
ten.unlocks: The engine stops resting on one legend: draw, ramp and counters from a permanent removal answers far less easily.

ten.why: The recon calls it the archetype-specific engine — 50% of the upgraded lists: every spell cast outside its caster's turn draws, which pays this deck on three of every four turns while a sorcery-speed pod collects nothing. It is symmetric: an instant-heavy opponent draws too, and that is the honest price.
ten.unlocks: The draw-go posture itself becomes card advantage — each ambush cast cantrips, ungated by power or combat.

ten.why: The diagnosis's first single point of failure is the commander himself — without him every trap is a full-price sorcery-speed creature — and it names Yeva as the only card that would replicate the flash half; she also lifts the one-creature-per-turn limit the recon lists as the commander's known failure mode.
ten.unlocks: The posture survives Radagast being answered twice, and with both out the second and third creatures of a turn also ambush.

ten.why: The field's named 'obvious power add' and a confirmed Game Changer: untapping in every other untap step converts the once-a-round ambush into four full-price casts per cycle, the largest single multiplier on the 3.638-bodies figure. Sleeving it moves the computed floor from 1 to 3 — exactly the target, and a pod conversation before it is a purchase.
ten.unlocks: A power door rather than a gap-filler: the deck's whole mana base works on everyone's turn. The floor lands on 3; whether the pod reads a Muse deck as bracket 3 is the table's call, not the calculator's.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite landfall triggers; infinite tapped land tokens

ten.why: Held out of the 99 by the bracket-3 target: the combo index records a two-card infinite with Tireless Provisioner, who is in the deck, so sleeving it moves the computed floor from 1 to 4 — and it sits in the build's own pool file.
ten.unlocks: The bracket-4 door: bestowed on any body it makes a copy or an Insect on every land drop at bracket-3 tempo, and the recorded infinite waits behind it. The line needs a stack scenario before it is claimed as a kill.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite landfall triggers; infinite tapped land tokens

ten.why: The other half of the benched pair, also in the pool file: alone it moves no bracket signal and no weak axis — ramp already reads six over the band — and its recorded infinite needs Springheart, so it matters only if both come in together.
ten.unlocks: Mana on every land drop, an Elf or Elemental to hand on the second — and the second key to the bracket-4 door. Unverified until a stack scenario runs the loop.

gaps: Ezuri's Predation is the diagnosis's own open question: the better sweeper for a 35-creature deck (a wipe that leaves 4/4 bodies) but filed threat:tokens, invisible to the axis. Whiptongue took the ranked slot because its claim is measurable; research-strategy settles whether the axis-invisible card is the right purchase.

End-Raze Forerunners left the ten: the diagnosis prices the finisher class adequate at four and moves the bind to board width, and stack 005 refuted the end-step-finisher line its ambush framing leaned on — a fifth overrun copy buys redundancy on a component that is not the thinnest.
Scavenging Ooze left for the marginal-frame reason: Deathgorge Scavenger now covers the graveyard class in the 99, so a second graveyard answer doubles a covered class before any uncovered one.

The Springheart + Tireless Provisioner line is the combo index's record and the index is format-agnostic; whether the loop's mana closes in this 99 needs a /resolve-stack run before anyone opens the bracket-4 door.

Whether Selvala's tapped mana can pay for a flashed cast in her own trigger window is an open diagnosis question settled by resolve-stack; its answer prices The Great Henge as backup versus upgrade, which could move Henge up this ranking.
Recon inclusion percentages describe first movers (~800 mostly-precon lists, 64 upgraded), not a settled meta — the 61/59/50/45% figures are leads the ranking uses, not verdicts.
